explorer.summary: Two growing blocks rebuilt by a Collatz-like map (K' = 3K/4 or 3K/4 + X) drive a short list of counters; when the first counter runs out the machine halts or builds much larger counters, depending on remainders; the first run-out (step 3.0·1023) did not halt, the next is due after about 10^(1011) steps; open.
explorer.verdict: The question is open, and probably out of reach. The tape is two growing blocks followed by a short list of counters. The first counter loses 1 every few epochs; when it runs out, the machine either halts (the halting configurations are proved in Lean) or turns one of its blocks into a new, much larger counter. Which of the two happens is decided by remainders of numbers produced by a Collatz-like map. The first run-out, at step 2.995·1023, did not halt; the second is due after about 10^(1011) steps, far beyond exact simulation.

explorer.summary: The left side is a long string of the 3-cell words 111 and 110; each round trip of the head replaces every word by the XOR of it and its right neighbour (rule 102), and defects (walls) come in from a small cycling structure at the right end. No closed tape language found yet.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. The sweep rule is now decoded: writing x = 111 and y = 110, one right sweep and one left sweep over a clean word string replace each word by the XOR of it and its right neighbour (x = 0, y = 1), the linear cellular automaton known as rule 102, checked exhaustively for every string up to 16 words. Every word string is therefore possible in the bulk, and halting depends only on the defects (alignment walls) that the small structure at the right end emits. No closed tape language has been found.

explorer.summary: A counter written in short runs of zeros at the left end, updated once per tick, while each tick the head zigzags across a long block of 1000000 that grows by about 3 every 7 ticks. Decided outside: busycoq PR 91 proves in Rocq that it halts (compiled here).
explorer.verdict: Decided by an outside Rocq proof: it halts. Busycoq pull request 91 (Alex Havrilla of DeepMind, 2026-11-17) proves this in Rocq, and we compiled it here with Coq 8.20.1 on busycoq's BB6 branch: it uses no axioms (Print Assumptions), and its transition table is this machine. It is their proof, on busycoq's definitions of a machine and of halting, and busycoq's maintainer has not yet reviewed it. Everything else on this page is what this repository found on its own, which by itself leaves the question open. The question is open. The tape is a short counter region at the left end, written as runs of zeros between 1s, followed by a long block (1000000)^n. Each tick the head zigzags left across the block, changes the counter near its right end, and sweeps back, and the block grows by about 3 every 7 ticks. The two sweeps are proved in Lean. The counter carries further left exponentially rarely, and its region grows like the logarithm of the time. Whether it ever produces the halting pattern (E reading 1) is not known.

explorer.summary: Blocks of 1s whose gaps (00 = 0, 000 = 1, single 0) are the digits of a binary counter; every visit of the right end is one leftward sweep and one rightward refill, and the ordinary visit (the counter goes down by one) is proved in Lean for any number of blocks; 36,604 of the 36,790 visits up to 10^9 steps are such instances, the rare others reload the counter; open. Accelerated run: no halt in 4.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. Every visit of the right end is one leftward sweep and one rightward refill. Lean proves how the sweep treats each block (for every length), that it can halt only at an odd block behind a single 0, and the whole ordinary visit, which decrements the counter, for any number of blocks. What is missing is an invariant: a description of the tapes that the rare reload visits produce, closed under every kind of visit. Simple local descriptions (which pairs or triples of neighbouring blocks occur) are not closed, so it must carry longer-range information.

explorer.summary: A block of N copies of 110 is moved across a junction two copies in, three out (N -> (3N+c)/2); the parity of N rewrites a 'wall' on the left that holds a tower of smaller 3/2-counters. Lean proves the step map for every wall (computed by a simulator that never looks at N) and the reduction to its orbit; no step that halts has been found. Accelerated run: no halt in 6.38e43391 steps.
explorer.verdict: The question is open, and reduced to an orbit. A step takes W A> 0 b^N 1 (b = 110) to W' A> 0 b^N' 1 with N' = (3N + c)/2, where the new wall W' and c are computed from the wall W and the parity of N. Lean proves the transfer loop behind the 3/2, the step map for every wall on which its simulator answers, and that, as long as it answers along the orbit, the machine halts from blank tape exactly when the orbit reaches a halting step. The map has been iterated for 40,000 steps without a halt (the plain-simulation map for 300,000), and no wall with a halting step has been found in a search of the wall graph: no halting mechanism is known for this machine, but no invariant excluding one is proved.

explorer.summary: A bouncer over the background 1^8 00 / (011)^3 0 carrying gliders: each event at the slow right end makes the left end emit a glider, gliders drift right, merge, and trigger the next event; halting needs a C>1 at the left end.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. The head shuttles out from the left end over a periodic background, rewriting the word 1^8 00 as (011)^3 0 on the way right and back on the way left (shift rules proved in Lean). It turns back at the first defect of the background or passes it, depending on the defect's current shape, so the defects work like the digits of a counter, and the far right end is reached only when all of them let the head through. The defects also move, as gliders between a glider gun at the left end and a slowly growing structure at the right end. No map between macro configurations is known yet, so neither halting nor non-halting is in reach.

Between rebuilds the machine is a binary counter that applies one fixed operation to a list of blocks once per tick, and the list is the binary expansion of the time it has left (checked against the machine, not proved). Rebuilds are still simulated cell by cell. With this the run passes 986 rebuilds, more than 1031,896 steps, without a halt (before: three rebuilds, 3·1010 steps). explorer.group: halving rounds with a power-of-two halt condition
explorer.summary: The tape is a list of blocks a^x; each round halves blocks from the left with a carry and pours the halves to the right (a single block x goes to (3x+5)/2 when odd). It halts iff a first block reaches 1, i.e. x0+3 is a power of two at the start of a run of odd rounds. Exact round map computed and checked; no halt in 1,000,000 rounds (> 10^94,000 steps).
explorer.verdict: The question is open, and Collatz-like. At every visit of the left end the tape is a list of blocks ax0 110 ax1 110 … (a = 01). A round halves blocks from the left as long as a carry survives and pours the halves into the blocks on the right: a single block x becomes (3x+5)/2 when odd and [x/2−1, 0, x] when even, an odd first block x0 becomes (x0−3)/2. Lean proves that a first block of 1 halts the machine, so it halts if and only if a run of odd rounds starts with x0+3 a power of two (as far as the computed round map is right: it is checked against the machine, not proved). The map has been iterated for 1,000,000 rounds from blank tape, more than 1094,000 steps, without a halt.

The run is understood at the level of passes: between two visits of the head to the wall the list of blocks changes by a short recursive rule, and every one of the 1,311,505 wall visits in the first 109 steps follows it (C simulator plus py/passmap.py, not a proof). ai.note: A translated counter in base 4, with lazy carries.

explorer.summary: One drain mechanism at every scale: a block of 1s is drained into pairs, the same sweep runs a ternary counter, and a drain of the wrong parity wipes its block into a gap where a copy of the whole run restarts; it halts only if a gap has one of a sparse set of fatal sizes (3, 29, 75, 115, 289, ...), open and Collatz-like. Accelerated run: no halt in 2.37e28 steps.
explorer.verdict: The question is open, and Collatz-like. The machine is a single drain mechanism used at every scale, and every rule of it is proved in Lean for all sizes and chained into one map, together with the two ways it can halt: a drain that ends exactly three cells short of the block on its right. At the top level that cannot happen; inside the gaps the run makes it happens for a sparse set of gap sizes (3, 29, 75, 115, 289, …), and whether the run ever makes a gap of such a size is a question about its own counter. Since 12 November there is also a reduction with nothing assumed: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if a hybrid map halts, which is the chained map wherever its rules apply and plain machine steps on the nodes they do not cover (halts_iff_hybrid; no uncovered node in the first 3·107 nodes).

explorer.summary: Antihydra: halts iff the walk x → ⌊3x/2⌋, with a counter +2 for even x and −1 for odd x, ever drives the counter below 0 (proved equivalent in Lean); open, and heuristically never. Accelerated run: no halt in 2.05e41681 steps.
explorer.verdict: The question is open, and is now a question about numbers. Lean proves (halts_iff, kernel) that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of (2, 7) under the map (p, a) ↦ (p + 2, 3k + 4) for a = 2k + 1, (p − 1, 3k + 2) for a = 2k ever meets an even a with p = 0. Why nobody expects a halt. The parity of a behaves like a fair coin, so p is a random walk with steps +2 and −1 and an upward drift of ½ per step. After 106 steps of the walk (a computation, not a proof) p is 498,505; a walk of that kind started at height p ever reaches −1 with probability about 0.618p+1. Deciding it would need control of the parity sequence of ⌊3x/2⌋ iterates, a famously hard problem (Mahler's 3/2 problem is of this kind).

At the end of a round the tape is 01001000 (01)^B T with a big block of B pairs and a short tail T. There are 1,144 classes of such tapes (one of 62 tails, B = r0 + m·x with m = 27, 45, 48 or 66 and r0 ≥ 20,000) such that every tape of a class ends its next round in a class again; the real run enters the set at B = 28,531. In Lean, a symbolic executor whose every move is proved to be a run of the machine (kernel) runs one round for each class with x free, and the arrival from blank tape; a second proved test shows that every round end announced lies in a class. The 1,144 rounds (133 million executor moves), the arrival and the six cycle rules are evaluated by native_decide, so the result rests on the Lean kernel and the Lean compiler. It is their proof, on busycoq's definitions of a machine and of halting, and busycoq's maintainer has not yet reviewed it. The run is a sequence of phases: a counter n becomes 8·(n div 3) + d, where the residue of n mod 3 and a word P of blocks to its left decide d and the next word. Lean proves the rounds of a phase for all lengths, and the residue-0 phase end: (L 0 1a+1 0, 3m + 3) → (L 0, a + 8m + 11). No halting transition was found in the word dynamics (trusted, by simulation), so the machine may well run forever, but the word dynamics is unbounded and not understood. Update, 13 November 2026: a search of all tails of at most 26 cells with the generic class map finds halting classes; the nearest needs 108 prescribed residues mod 3 in a row from the start of the run (observed, not proved). explorer.verdict: The machine halts (Lean theorem halts; two steps of it by compiled evaluation). At the visits of the right end the tape is a short front, a ladder of levels (a rung of n blocks 0111111111 and one of eight separator words) and a tail at the left end. Every level is a digit with 16 positions: a hit from the right moves it to the next position, at ten positions the hit is absorbed, at six it is passed on to the left. What lies left of a level therefore lives exactly as it would right behind the front, only 8/3 times slower. After the reset of step 27,167,343, which turned the old ladder into fuel, the tail eats two fuel blocks and leaves three new levels in every 12 hits. With 887 levels the fuel is used up, the next hit runs into the blank left end, and state C reads a 0: the halt, at a step with 759 digits.

Its first four rules are those of the three machines that busycoq PR59 proves to halt in round 161,211 on the block 1011; this machine rewrites 1011 to 0001 instead and, in an accelerated run (computed, not proved), carries on: no halt up to round 200,000. Every time the head turns left into D the tape is X(a,b,c) = 1^a 0 (10)^b 1 D> 0 1^c, the same with 00 (Y), or Z(a,c) = 1^a 0 D> 0 1^c. Lean proves the 20 rules that take each shape to the next, for all values, and (kernel only, halts_iff in lean/Model.lean) that the machine halts from blank tape exactly when the orbit of X(2,0,3) reaches some Z(a,2). That needs a run of the Y rule whose middle block empties exactly when the right block holds 3 ones: impossible by parity in the doubling stage of a round, a chance of about 1/N elsewhere. 2,000 rounds of the map (N about 10756, about 101511 steps) show no halt.

explorer.summary: A 4/3 map on a run of 1s whose tail list holds a second counter that drains the main one: it halts exactly if that counter reaches four times the main run, which needs an astronomically long streak of m mod 3 ≠ 1; probviously non-halting, and no regular invariant can prove it. Accelerated run: no halt in 1.21e38782 steps.
explorer.verdict: Open; the whole map is now known and no halt is in sight. Sample the run when the head is in state E at the left end reading 1: the tape is EL(m, T) = E> 1 00 1^m T where T is a short list of runs 0 1^a1 0 1^a2 …. One round sends m to (4m + c)/3 and T to T′, where c and T′ depend only on m mod 3 and T (once m is large compared with T). This exact round map matches every EL event of the direct run up to 5·109 steps and was iterated 100,000 rounds (past 1024990 steps) without a halt. The tail is mostly a single growing run that is absorbed into m whenever m ≡ 1 (mod 3); none of the 4,545 rounds tried, including synthetic tails, halts. Third pass. The halting condition is found: with the list T = [a, …], the first run a is swallowed when m = 1 mod 3 and otherwise grows by 4/3 while the main run pays, m′ = (4m − a)/3; the machine halts when a reaches 4m (+14). That needs about 4m/a rounds in a row without m = 1 mod 3, so it is probviously non-halting; and because a regular language cannot compare a with m, no closed tape language can prove it (the pushdown reduction fails with every DFA tried). No halt in 1018 steps by macro simulation.

Heuristically it never halts.

explorer.summary: An exact ternary counter, least significant digit at the left end, whose digits are pairs of long runs of alternating cells read mod 4; the increment is proved in Lean for every carry depth, and so is the shuttle that moves a run to the right end when a shrinking run runs out. Open: the whole transfer (it nests) and an invariant; tapes with the same residues and short runs do halt.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. The tape is an exact ternary counter: its digits are pairs of runs of alternating cells, valued by their lengths mod 4, and each trip of the head adds one. That increment is proved in Lean (kernel) for every carry depth, and it covers 99.86% of the trips in the first 3·1012 steps. The counter keeps shrinking one run of each digit; when such a run runs out, a transfer moves a long run to the right end of the tape, two cells per shuttle of the head. The shuttle itself is now proved in Lean for every list of runs in between and any number of shuttles, and so are the events at a run boundary, including the one pattern that halts. What is missing is the transfer as a whole (the shuttles before the tail is “saturated”, transfers nested inside transfers, the pairing of the digits afterwards) and an invariant. The invariant cannot be about residues alone: tapes with exactly the residues of a real configuration but several short runs do halt (for example 6 6 4 6 5 5 5 5 6 7 at step 5,943). In the real run every transfer of the first 1014 steps has long runs to spare, but that is an observation, not a proof.

explorer.verdict: The question is open. Lean proves two of the machine's fast moves and its halting situation (kernel) and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps. What it does. The tape has two regular parts. On the left a 26-cell word is repeated (w = 1111 000 1 000 1 000 111111 0 1 000), and the number of copies grows by one every few hundred thousand steps late in the run. On the right a finer pattern of short blocks grows too. Between them is an irregular boundary region where the head does its work in zig-zags of 50 to 100 cells; it never sweeps the whole tape in one go. Where a halt would come from. Only F reading a 1 halts, and F is entered from E reading a 0; so 1 0 D>1 halts (halt_D). In the first 2·106 steps D reads a 1 233,188 times, never with 1 0 to its left.

explorer.verdict: The question is open. Lean proves both passes over the bulk of the tape (kernel) and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps. What it does. Seen at the right end, the tape is a list of blocks (110)n separated by short separators (10, 1, 0 1). The leftward pass rewrites every 110 as 010 (seen from the left end the tape is blocks of (100)n), and the rightward pass turns them back. On each round trip the last block grows by two and the first few blocks are rewritten like the low digits of a counter; now and then the change runs further right, like a carry. Where a halt would come from. Only F reading a 0 halts, i.e. E standing on 1 0 (halt_E). In the run F always reads a 1.

explorer.summary: A list of counts written in stretches of 01: each round trip takes 3 from the first count while the rest of the list cycles through one of four periodic patterns, and when the first count runs out the second takes its place; Lean proves it never halts (kernel rounds, native_decide for the long runs).
explorer.verdict: It never halts. Lean proves nonhalting: from blank tape the machine reaches one of 62 tape templates and moves from template to template forever. The 62 round trips are checked by the kernel; the start and the 62 ends of an epoch (2.5 million symbolic moves) by native_decide. What it does. Each time B reaches the left end the tape reads B> 00 (01)a 000 (01)b 000 …, a list of counts separated by short words. The rightward sweep turns 010101 into 011001 and the leftward sweep turns it back. Each round trip takes 3 from a, while the end of the list runs through one of four periodic patterns (periods 15, 22, 16 and 9 round trips) and b gains 99, 141, 99 or 57 per period. When a is used up, b takes its place and a new, longer epoch begins: the first counts of successive epochs are 4, 12, 20, 38, 68, 122, 240, 484, 1002, 2104, 4375, …. Why it cannot halt. Only D reading a 0 halts, after C>1 0. Every round trip of every pattern and every way an epoch can end has been checked as a symbolic run with the counts as variables, and each lands on a template again; a potential on the counts shows that an epoch always ends with the second count large enough for those runs.

The whole run is now one rule: the tape is a binary counter with doublers (words 1010, 000, 100), and each round sends one defect through it. A tape with one defect cannot halt; a halt needs two defects to meet. [1 a^dk x^nk] 1: blocks of x with a ternary digit d in front of each. One round trip of the head is a ternary decrement: the first nonzero digit drops by one, the zeros below it become 2, every block the borrow passes loses one x and the first block gains one. When the counter runs out a new round starts with one more block. Every rule is proved in Lean for all sizes, and the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the counter model reaches a halting pattern: the borrow meeting an empty block followed by a block with digit 0 (halts_iff_model, kernel-checked). Since 12 November the theorem has no hypothesis: the model is a function defined on every list of blocks, including the patterns that never show up in the run, and each of its cases is proved to be what the machine does. The model has run 332,875 rounds (more than 10292 steps) without halting. A halt needs a charged pair of blocks, two neighbours whose block length and digit do not match mod 3 (Lean, good_not_halt). A round-skipping simulator, tested round by round

An exact accelerated run of the rule (checked against the machine) reaches 104000 steps with no halt. A halt can only happen at a jump, and only if three block lengths satisfy an exact equation (for example x = z0/2 + 2); in the run they never come close, and nothing found so far rules the coincidence out, so the machine is very likely non-halting but a proof looks Collatz-hard.

The tape holds a counter (100)^n and a list of runs of 1s of lengths 7, 13, 19, … (6k+1). The run goes in epochs: in each, the number of runs of every length is halved and they move up one length, half the counter becomes new runs of 7, and the new counter is about 5/2 times the old number of runs of 7; so everything grows by 5/4 every two epochs, and the step count by 25/16. The machine halts exactly when state B reads 0 1 1 1 (B0 C1 E1 put F on a 1; the path is proved in Lean). An exact accelerated simulator,

explorer.verdict: The question is open, and it is now a question about a small system of events, proved in Lean. The machine is a counter ticked once per round trip across a growing wall, and the tick is a carry automaton on the counter's digits. When a carry runs through all the digits it reads the last cell, and one of four things happens, each proved for every wall and every digit string: the last cell is set, the counter gains a digit, the whole wall is turned into counter digits, or the machine halts. So the machine halts from blank tape exactly when this event system reaches a halting event (kernel only). In the run from blank tape the first such event comes about 1.96·1020 steps in and turns a wall of 8,072,508,833 pairs into digits; the next one is of the order of 22.5·109 sweeps later, and which kind it is is not known.

F is entered only from E reading a 1, and E only from D reading a 0; so a halt needs the head in D on 0 1 1 (and as D is entered only from A reading a 1, the head in A on 1 0 1 1). explorer.summary: A one-number map n → 3n − 2c_i + i + 3 between thresholds c_i = 10·2^i − i − 7; halts iff the orbit of 1 lands exactly on a threshold (reduction proved in Lean). Not hit in 1.25·10^6 map steps. Accelerated run: no halt in 3.26e1492 steps.
explorer.verdict: The question is open, and reduced to a map on one number. Lean proves (kernel, no native_decide) that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of 1 under the map next reaches none. In closed form the map is n → 3n − 2ci + i + 3 for ci < n < ci+1, with ci = 10·2i − i − 7, and it halts exactly when n = ci+1. Iterated 1,250,000 times, the orbit never lands on a threshold; n then has about 833,000 binary digits. A probability argument says a hit is ever less likely (about 1/2i per step), so the machine is expected never to halt, but no proof is known.

explorer.summary: A counter (1^2 0)^m at the left end whose overflows come at doubling times; the overflow at length m rewrites the word W only in a window starting exactly at digit m - 1, as if W held a number to which the counter adds what it counted; when the window reaches the end W is rebuilt. explorer.verdict: The question is open. Lean proves that the machine can halt only by stepping, in state F, onto the blank region right of everything written (kernel, from a closed tape language), and that there is no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1011 steps. What it does. At each overflow the tape reads A>0 1 0 (1^2 0)^m 1^4 0 W (the block 1^4 is longer near restructures). m grows by one per overflow and the gap between overflows doubles (within 0.5% at 20 of the 24 overflows from step 100,161 on). Between overflows W changes only in a window that moves right through it. Restructures, where W is rebuilt, came at about 55,000 steps and between 2.5·1010 and 3.1·1010 steps. Why it is hard. The halt needs the head to come to the right end in state F; that would happen at a restructure, and the rule that rebuilds W has not been worked out.

Lean (kernel) proves the six regular macro steps and the two main shapes of the anomaly for all parameter values, and no halt in the first 10,000 steps (107 with native_decide). Lean also shows that the pattern of the word and of the gaps is not an invariant by itself: a short Q configuration of the same form halts after 190 steps. Non-halting therefore depends on sizes: every collision cascade must end before the word runs out. In the simulated run it is always won, by at least 1.0 bits. Update, 12 November. Lean now also proves this machine's own form of the anomaly with a one-unit counter, 12 collision rules, and a partial macro map (a function from one word-and-counter configuration to the next, proved to be followed by the machine wherever it is defined). The map is far from complete: of the 270 collisions in the simulated run, 43 follow a proved rule. For the sister machine 1RB0RF_1LC1RE_0LD0LC_1RD0RB_1RA0RB_0LC--- the map is complete; here the collisions have many more cases, and they keep a misaligned gap alive instead of clearing it.

Its run is a clock at the right end of the tape: a block of 1s grows by four cells per tick and tick k sends the word beside it through 2k trips of the head — proved in Lean for every k and every word, whenever the 2k trips all return. Between clock phases a second clock, on the next block in, takes over; it is not yet proved. An exact accelerated run follows the machine to step 2.39·10248 without a halt.

explorer.summary: Space Needle: halts iff Doucette's sequence 6, 10, 17, 41, 101, ... (D -> D + v + 3a for D = 2^v(2a+1)) hits a power of two; proved equivalent in Lean, probviously non-halting. Accelerated run: no halt in 3.30e22 steps.
explorer.verdict: The question is open, and equivalent to a question about a simple sequence. Lean proves, checked by the kernel alone, that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some term of the sequence D0 = 6, Dk+1 = Dk + v + 3a, where Dk = 2v(2a+1), is a power of two (halts_iff_pow2). None of the first 300,000 terms is (Lean, native_decide; the first 20,000 by the kernel), nor of the first 3·106 (C). The terms grow by a factor of about 1.92 per step and their number of factors 2 stays small (at most 24 so far), so a power of two would be an extraordinary coincidence: the machine is probviously non-halting. A proof would need control of the 2-adic valuations of a sequence defined by additions, which is beyond current methods.

explorer_family: G06: one side stops, the other square-root (fixed/sqrt)

ai.note: Its halting reduces to a Collatz-like question.

explorer.summary: An alternating tape cut into blocks by single separator cells. Each round trip from the right end is a tick that flips separators by a few rules depending on the parities of the blocks, like an odometer; now and then a tick reaches the left end and rebuilds the front of the list, and the whole pattern recurs on larger scales. Open. Accelerated run: no halt in 1.26e17 steps.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the sweeps, the ticks of the two common families for chains of any length and blocks of any size, one rebuild for every length of its last block, and that every halt must come from B>0 1 1 (kernel). It also proves no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide). A C program checks the block form at all 30,932 right-end turns of the first 1010 steps. What it does. The tape is 1010… cut into blocks (10)n by single extra cells, the separators (1 or 0). A round trip from the right end, a tick, sweeps left over some separators, turns at one, and sweeps back, complementing everything it crosses. Which separator it turns at, and how the block lengths change, depends on the separators and the parities of the blocks; two families of rules cover 30,528 of the 30,932 ticks of the first 1010 steps. The last block grows by one or two each tick, so the right edge grows smoothly. The rebuilds. 238 of those ticks reach the left end instead. There the head works for a long time and rebuilds the front of the list; the same sequences of lists then recur with more blocks on the right, on larger and larger scales. Where a halt would come from. Only F reading a 1 halts.

explorer.summary: A nested ternary counter: the tape is a list of segments of 111-blocks drained by 3j per event; segments run out one after another (collapses), and after each the counter settles into a new regime of the same kind. Exact runs pass collapses at 2.5×1018, 2.06×1035, 2.58×1054 and 2.8–3.0×1054 steps without halting 4.8×1054 and 12 more middle collapses, and reach 1.65×1064.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. At each new cell on the right the tape is 2 3^16 5 3 5 3^a1 5 3^a2 ... 5 3^am TAIL (lengths of runs of 1s), and the counts ai follow a closed-form law Pn → Qn → Rn → Pn+1, checked against direct simulation on every event to 109 steps. An exact model of the whole tape as one ternary counter follows the machine through the first collapse (2.5×1018 steps) and the middle collapse at 2.06×1035; a lean accelerator (17 November 2026) carries it on through a second middle collapse at 2.58×1054 steps and the collapse of the third regime's oldest segment (2.8×1054 to 3.0×1054; the end counter goes 126 → 127), and on (18 November) through 12 more middle collapses and the end counter running out at 4.8×1054 (124 blocks, merged into the oldest segment (290 → 414)) to 1.65×1064 steps, with no halt. The oldest segment now holds 391 blocks.

explorer.verdict: The question is open, and reduced to a map on pairs of numbers. Lean proves (kernel, no native_decide) that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of (2, 1) under the map f below reaches a pair with r = p + 1. Iterating the map 3,000,000 times, the orbit never does; by then p and r have about 650,000 binary digits, so the machine has run for more than 2650000 steps. A probability argument says a hit becomes ever less likely (the chance at each decision is about 1/p), so the machine is expected never to halt, but no proof is known.

Where a halt would come from. Every rightward run is a pass that crosses gaps (runs of 0s between two 1s) of length 1 and 2 and stops at the first other gap. Lean proves that the pass halts exactly when that gap has length 3 (pass_outcome, kernel). Why it has not halted. Lean proves that the run is a macro machine on lists of numbers, and that the machine halts only if the macro machine gets stuck. That needs two 1s side by side next to an empty segment, which only odd numbers can bring about; in the run they are rare (at most 4 at a time), and the macro machine has never been stuck in 1010 steps. Is that luck or structure? Configurations one even number away from the run's do get stuck, and per flip the run looks just like them: at their stuck rate it would have got stuck with probability about 0.17 so far. No structural reason for it to stay unstuck has shown up.

The left part of the tape is a binary counter written as a composition of s into parts (gaps 1 1 0^(5a-2)); every tick of it adds 1 to a binary number N written on the right. explorer.verdict: The question is open. The machine halts exactly from F> 0 0 0 (both directions in Lean). The run is a sequence of periods: in each the head goes to the left end and back, and at the right end the big block grows by four 1s (a 21-step rule proved in Lean). The periods double: 459,930, 919,858, ..., 58,870,786 steps, each exactly twice the previous minus 2, and later 3,759,931,386 and 7,519,862,778 steps, with occasional larger corrections when the digits near the left end change. F has met 0 0 1 only at steps 257, 11,457, 16,839,809 and 2,371,684,619, the only times up to that step (5 times in 1010 steps by the ctxcount census), each time just after a long block was written at the very left end of the tape; the halt needs a 0 where those near misses had the 1.

explorer.verdict: Decided by an outside Rocq proof: it halts. Busycoq pull request 84 (Alex Havrilla of DeepMind, 2026-11-17) proves this in Rocq, and we compiled it here with Coq 8.20.1 on busycoq's BB6 branch: it uses no axioms (Print Assumptions), and its transition table is this machine. It is their proof, on busycoq's definitions of a machine and of halting, and busycoq's maintainer has not yet reviewed it. Everything else on this page is what this repository found on its own, which by itself leaves the question open. The question is open. The macro structure is identified by simulation (rounds that halve every run of equal blocks); Lean proves the shift rules the sweeps are made of and that a halt can only come from 1 1 1 D> 0. In 109 steps D read a 0 about 21,000 times and every time the left neighbours were 1 1 0 or blank, one cell short of a halt.

It can halt only during a rare event, the merger of two walls; every merger type tried symbolically (both walls in any of their six shapes, 0 to 2 blocks apart) ends without halting, and the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1010 steps. A proof would have to cover every merger and edge event; that has not been done.

explorer.summary: A few huge blocks of 1s. An exact event map is proved in Lean: an even block is split, a quarter to the left and three quarters to the right; an odd block at the left end is folded, 2 for 3. The machine halts iff the orbit of this map leaves the rules and stops; no halt in the first 10^137 steps (kernel), 10^13275 (compiled). Open.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. The tape is a few huge blocks of 1s, and everything the machine does is arithmetic on their lengths: an even block is split, a quarter going left and three quarters going right; odd blocks are glued to their neighbours; an odd block at the left end is folded, every 2 ones becoming 3. Lean proves these rules for every size, proves that the machine halts if and only if the orbit of the resulting map reaches a halting configuration, and proves that there is no halt in the first 10137 steps (1013275 by compiled evaluation). Whether the rules go on for ever is not known: it depends on remainders modulo 4 of numbers that keep being multiplied by 3/4 and 3/2.

A short word w at the left end is a memory: the next w and the exact correction depend only on w and the parity of k, by a table read off simulation. The machine halts exactly when w reaches a pattern with four ones in a row together with the wrong parity of k. The orbit avoids it for 2,000,005 half-phases; with random parities it is reached after about 240 half-phases.

A particle system on the background (1110)n: walls drift left and become runners at the left end, the head shuttles between the left end and the first runner, runners pass walls and merge in pairs into new walls; a halt needs three 0s in a row inside the tape, never seen in 1.2·1011 steps. explorer.summary: A binary counter in six-cell units whose overflows rewrite an irregular left part; rarely an overflow reaches the left end, the old counter freezes into blocks and the wall becomes a far longer counter. Lean proves the run through the first such event (no halt in the first 8^(p0+1) steps, p0 about 3.2e23); the next three are computed, and the left part behaves chaotically, so the question stays op
explorer.verdict: The question is open. The machine is a binary counter: left of a periodic wall the tape reads as six-cell units holding one or two bits, and every three sweeps add one. When the counter is full, the carry rewrites the left part of the tape and the counting starts over. Rarely the carry runs to the left end (an S event): the old counter freezes into blocks and the wall, by then astronomically long, becomes the new counter. Lean proves every rule on the way from blank tape through the first S event, for all counter and wall lengths: no halt in the first 8p0+1 steps, p0 = 321,163,084,821,590,067,792,163 (a number with about 2.9·1023 digits). A trusted simulator gets through the next three S events without a halt. Each S event is a new, apparently random trial for halting, and the left part never settles into a pattern.

ai.note: A wide shift-overflow bouncer counter.

explorer.summary: Marker counter (class IV): a base-5 counter of markers between 0010-blocks, whose markers drift and merge; halting needs two merges close together. No halt in 10^16 steps.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. The machine runs a base-5 counter written as markers between blocks; Lean proves its regular sweeps for all block lengths, and an exact fast simulator finds no halt in 1016 steps. It can only halt if two of the rare merges of drifting markers happen close together, which nothing here decides. Family F05. One of 40 holdouts on the same five-state core; the family's exact block-list map runs this machine for 1.4·10200 steps without a halt. Twin. Proved in Lean to share one question with 1RB0LC_0RC1RF_1RD0RE_1LE0RA_0LA0LE_1RB---: both runs meet a bad F-entry together, and if they never do, the two machines halt together.

ai.note: Near copy of a proved machine or a Skelet #1 sibling: one table entry differs, and it stops firing after about 1e8 steps.

explorer.summary: The reservoir is a chain of independent mod-4 counters (decoded, with an exact accelerator): the third far-end contact comes at visit 2.80e36 (step 2.35e73) and does not halt; Lean proves a halt can only happen on blank tape beyond the far end; the next contact needs more than (4/3)^(4.67e35) sweeps.
explorer.verdict: The question is open, but the machine is now well understood. Behind a block of 1s that grows by two each sweep sits a chain of small counters that each count 0, 1, 2, 3, followed by a chaotic tail. The chain is exactly predictable, so the run was followed, with exact step counts, through 2.80·1036 sweeps (2.35·1073 steps): no halt, and the third event turned the block into a chain of 4.67·1035 counters. Lean proves that the machine can only halt on the blank tape beyond the far end, which the head will not see again for more than (4/3)4.67·10^35 sweeps. Whether that contact, or a later one, halts depends on the chaotic tail.

ai.note: Its nearest proved neighbours halt, so a halt here is possible.

explorer.summary: Bouncer whose tape is mostly one 51-cell word repeated, with a run (101)^a on the left and short irregular zones at both ends of the repeated part; it halts only if D reads 0 with a 0 on its left, never seen.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the exact way a halt would happen (D reading 0 with a 0 on its left) and five shift rules; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1011 steps, and in 3·109 steps the cell left of D, when D reads 0, has always been 1. The irregular zones are not understood.

explorer_family: G08: two-sided square-root growth (sqrt/sqrt)

ai.note: A bouncer with a chaotic edge.

explorer.summary: Two blocks, (10)^x and 1^y, take turns doubling at each other's expense; it halts only if an all-ones tape 1^n ever has n = 32·2^k − 2k − 12 (or one of a few values below 40), and that has not happened. Accelerated run: no halt in 8.16e23 steps.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; an exact macro simulator finds no halt in the first 1015 steps. Lean proves the left phase rule (below) for all sizes. What Lean proves. The whole phase map, every case for all sizes (E(x, z) = E>0 (10)^x 1^z, R(x, y) = (10)^x 1^y C>0 and the bounce frame Q(m, k, t) = (10)^m 1 A>0 0 (10)^k 1^t), and halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the map, iterated from R(0, 2), which the blank tape reaches in 2 steps,, reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1). By native_decide the first 108 phases (about 4.1·1021 machine steps) do not. Lean also proves that the even phases lead only to even phases or to an all-ones tape, and checks, for every all-ones tape of length n < 105, that its run halts before the next even phase or all-ones tape exactly when n is 0, 6 or 32·2k − 2k − 12 (20, 50, 112, 238, …). What is not proved: that this list holds for every n, and that the run never lands on it. Where a halt would come from. F0 halts, and F is entered only from E0: E stands on the 0 at the left end and walks right with F over 0101…, so a halt needs at most one 1 a

ai.note: Our experiments suggest the outcome turns on chaotic digits.

explorer.summary: A list of blocks of 1s; each block gives half of itself to each neighbour, the head moving on when its length is odd and turning back when it is even. Lean proves that the machine halts iff the orbit of an explicit map on the block list halts, which needs a last block of 2^k - 1 ones; no halt in 2.6·10^27 steps.
explorer.verdict: Open, Collatz-like, reduced in Lean to an explicit map. It is a Lean theorem (kernel-checked) that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of one configuration under an explicit map G on lists of block lengths halts. The tape is a list of blocks of 1s; the head splits each block in two halves, moving on to the next block when the length is odd and turning back when it is even. It halts exactly when it gets to the right end of the tape and the last block has 2k − 1 ones. explorer_family: G10: other power on one side (power/sqrt, linear/*)

ai.note: Our experiments suggest the outcome turns on chaotic digits.

explorer.summary: Rewrites a tape of 110 and 1111 words in an irregular way; grows about 100 cells per tenfold time.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1010 steps. Where a halt would come from. The machine halts only in state B reading 1, and B is entered only from A reading 0 and stepping right (1RB). In the first 108 steps that happens 3,447,235 times and B always reads a 0. Why it is hard. No counter or repeating cycle has shown up: macro machines with blocks of 2 to 6 cells do not compress the run (with blocks of k cells, about one macro step per k steps), and the contents of the tape look irregular. A finite-automaton invariant (CTL) with windows of up to 8 cells does not close. A proof would need an invariant that captures why the halting pattern never forms, and none is known.

ai.note: A bit-level cellular automaton with a controller: one sweep sends a word to its running XOR with an alternating bit. Exact on every round checked, not proved.

explorer.summary: Blocks of 1s on both sides of the head; a long block next to an empty one is dismantled, half to each neighbour, ending in 2 or 3 ones by parity. It is a Lean theorem (kernel-checked) that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of one configuration under an explicit map G on two lists of block lengths halts. The tape is a list of blocks of 1s with the head between two of them; a long block next to an empty one is dismantled two 1s at a time, half going to each neighbour, down to 2 or 3 ones by its parity. The machine halts exactly when the blocks left of the head are used up, which needs every one of them to be 111 at the same moment; for a lone block that means 3·(2m − 1) ones. explorer.summary: A wall of 0s is eaten three cells per sweep while a block of 10s grows by two; each wall maps (3k+r, y) to (4k+c, y+d) with (c, d) = (1, +4), (5, +6), (8, −1), a Collatz-like map whose counter y drifts upward; proved in Lean that it never halts unless y ever reaches 0 at a z not divisible by 3.
explorer.verdict: The question is open, and reduced in Lean to a Collatz-like orbit. The machine follows (Lean, kernel) the map (3k, y) → (4k+1, y+4), (3k+1, y) → (4k+5, y+6), (3k+2, y) → (4k+8, y−1) on its walls, and never halts as long as that orbit, started at (0, 0), never reaches y = 0 with z not a multiple of 3 (not_halts_of_orbit). With native_decide: the first 10,000 macro steps stay inside the rules, so no halt in the first 102400 steps. Why it has not halted. b is odd for long stretches (an odd b can never become 0), and the even stretches are short chains of doublings, each with a chance of order 1/width to hit 0. explorer.verdict: The question is open. The machine is a binary counter that gains 39 or 42 every 8 sweeps. Lean proves that every sweep keeps the counter in its steady form except at a B-overflow (once every second doubling), so a halt would have to come out of a B-overflow transient; the run through the first one is evaluated too. A dedicated pass decoded the transient completely: for about 3·2w bounces the binary counter runs against a base-3 counter written over the long block, and then a short clean-up loop has to bring the block back to zeros. The digits the transient leaves behind depend on the width in a number-theoretic way, the block is not safe under arbitrary orders of operations, and one digit pattern makes the clean-up long. So the missing lemma is not a routine induction. An exact accelerated simulation shows 16 transients (to 1.1·1017 steps) all recovering, with no halt.

explorer.verdict: It halts, proved in Coq (theorem halt : halts tm c0 on busycoq's definitions, no axioms). The proof is DeepMind's fast engine of busycoq PR 93, built for the table one transition away, with the four rules that pass through that transition changed and every proof built on them redone. Run from blank tape, the proved engine reaches a halting configuration (F on a 1) after 261,156 of its steps, on a tape of about 22410 cells; no simulator could get there step by step. What it does. The tape holds a counter (100)^n and a list of runs of 1s of lengths 7, 13, 19, … (6k+1). The run goes in epochs: in each, the number of runs of every length is halved and they move up one length, half the counter becomes new runs of 7, and the new counter is about 5/2 times the old number of runs of 7; so everything grows by 5/4 every two epochs, and the step count by 25/16. These rules hold only up to small corrections (a run more or less, odd runs between the groups), which is why the community calls this a chaotic Bell. explorer.verdict: The question is open. Left of the start the tape is a block of 1011 words, which grows by one word every two rounds, then a binary counter (about three cells a bit), then junk: a run of 1110 words and a second, slower counter. Lean proves the left-end turns and the counter's two carries for all lengths, and that a counter of 2m digits counts through all 4m values (count). Each overflow of the counter eats one or two junk words; when the junk is used up the machine restarts: the whole block turns into junk and the counter into the new slow counter. The blank-tape run restarts at round 25,515,382 with 12,757,674 words of new junk. Jumping from overflow to overflow (checked against the machine at small sizes, extrapolated beyond) the next two epochs also end in restarts, not halts; the one after that starts with a junk length of about 217,010,257 words, and whether it halts depends on arithmetic properties of that number that are out of reach. Halting configurations do exist in the same family, so no closed family of configurations avoids them without that arithmetic.

The first two cycles do not halt. The orbit resets at phases 8 and 6,819; at phase 6,819 the stack has more than 102900 words, so the machine runs at least 102899 steps without halting (runs_long, lean/Orbit.lean, by native_decide). Deciding the third cycle needs about 5·102901 phases of the map: out of reach by simulation. Heuristically it halts, absurdly late. If the residues mod 3 behave like coin flips, each cycle ends in a halt with probability 1/5 (simulated: 0.19 to 0.20 over 4,000 random cycles from large random starts), so the machine halts with probability 1, but each cycle is exponentially longer than the one before: a halt would come after a tower of exponentials of steps.

The run is understood as a nested odometer whose regular rounds are proved in Lean, but its irregular events (blocks running empty) are only observed, not proved to come from a closed list; nothing like a proof of non-halting is in sight. Where a halt would have to come from. The machine halts only in F reading a 1, and F is entered only from E reading a 1, right after D wrote a 1 on a 0: so a halt needs D>0 1 1 somewhere. In the run F is entered only 3 times in the first 2·109 steps (first at step 49,249), always when two g4 gadgets meet across an empty block (or at a gadget made by such an event), and it always reads a 0. No closed set of shapes. The irregular gadgets form a closed alphabet, but the tape language they span contains halting tapes: the trap 101, and a tape of regular gadgets with every block of length ≥ 2 that halts (both proved in Lean). So the decision has to come from relations between block lengths, which no shape-level (CTL-style) argument captures. Pushed to 2.77·1017 steps. explorer.verdict: The question is open. The run is understood as a nested odometer whose regular rounds are proved in Lean, but its irregular events (blocks running empty) are only observed, not proved to come from a closed list; nothing like a proof of non-halting is in sight. Where a halt would have to come from. The machine halts only in F reading a 1, and F is entered only from E reading a 1, right after D wrote a 1 on a 0: so a halt needs D>0 1 1 somewhere. In the run F is entered only 5 times in the first 2·109 steps (first at step 49,249), always when two g4 gadgets meet across an empty block (or at a gadget made by such an event), and it always reads a 0. No closed set of shapes. The irregular gadgets form a closed alphabet, but the tape language they span contains halting tapes: the trap 101, and a tape of regular gadgets with every block of length ≥ 2 that halts (both proved in Lean). So the decision has to come from relations between block lengths, which no shape-level (CTL-style) argument captures. Pushed to 1.17·1017 steps. What P does to the word over many trips, and what happens when a trip does not come back (the end of a phase), is not proved. explorer_family: G11: slow on both sides (exp/fixed, exp/exp, exp/power)

ai.note: Open PR 48, by Dahoas, proves that it never halts. Not merged yet.

explorer.summary: Works in levels: a block (10111)^b is moved word by word to the left end, drained, and recycled as the next block, 2 to 6.6 times as long. For the four short tails the level map is exact (b' = (9b+c)/2 with the next tail chosen by b mod 4; proved visit by visit in Lean, composed symbolically for all b). Other levels count in binary between the blocks, and the next level then depends on the digits.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. The run is a sequence of levels, each about 2 to 6.6 times as long as the one before. Every single visit of the left end in the common phases is a Lean theorem for all block sizes, and for the four common level types the map from one level to the next is an exact formula. But some levels contain a binary counter, and what follows them depends on the binary digits of a block length; no closed description of those levels has been found. The machine halts exactly when the head, in state A, stands on a 0 followed by 1 0; that has not happened in 5.6·1015 steps.

ai.note: A Bell with an escalating refill: a counter that counts down and refills at growing levels.

explorer.summary: A long run of 10 pairs on the left grows steadily; behind it the tape is a word of 10-pair counters separated by two kinds of markers, 1^2 0 and 1 0^2, rewritten by sweeps.
explorer.verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps, the C simulator none in 109. The macro structure described below is observed in the simulation, not proved.

explorer_family: G13: other powers and bounded sides (power/power, fixed/*)

ai.note: Studied here for weeks. Detailed structure is known, but no complete proof.

explorer.summary: A chaotic counter eats a reservoir behind a growing block; far-end contacts (events) after sweeps 5, 9, 29, 137 and 167,887 (step 84,443,579,279) did not halt, the next is about 2^19,000 sweeps away, and in short-block models about a quarter of contacts halt.
explorer.verdict: The question is open, and looks out of reach. The machine applies one fixed map, sweep after sweep, to the region behind a block of 1s that grows by two each sweep; the region is a chaotic counter eating a reservoir. Each time the counter reaches the far end (so far after sweeps 5, 9, 29, 137 and 167,887) the block becomes a new reservoir: the last one has 335,504 cells, and at the measured 17 cells per doubling the next contact is about 219,000 sweeps away. The counter has no regular digits, so that contact cannot be predicted; in scaled-down models about one contact in four halts.

ai.note: Its nearest proved neighbours halt, so a halt here is possible.

explorer.summary: Epochs with exact doubling: the tape ends in (aaacacac)^T ... (baccaaa)^(6T+17) (a = 10, b = 100, c = 1000) and the next epoch has T' = 2T + 5 (checked for 9 epochs, 6·10^10 steps); phases 1, 2 and 5 of an epoch are proved in Lean for every count, phases 3 and 4 (an inner counter) are exact 144- and 288-visit cycles checked by symbolic computation; open.
explorer.verdict: The question is open, but the run is now known in detail: it goes through epochs whose sizes follow T' = 2T + 5 exactly, with X = 6T + 17 copies of the word baccaaa at each epoch start, 72T + 290 visits of the right end per epoch and (from T = 91 on) exactly 16416T² + 151769T + 288000 steps. Three of the five phases of every epoch are proved in Lean for all counts; the other two, where an inner counter runs deep inside the tape, are exact cycles of 144 and 288 visits checked by symbolic computation but not yet in Lean.

explorer.summary: Halts, proved in Coq: it runs like the T4 table from state A (a D0 detour can only add halts), and DeepMind's PR 93 engine changed for T4 reaches a halt from A after 350,227 engine steps (tape about 2^3562 cells). Rounds end at the left end with the tape a list of blocks 1^(6m+1) separated by 00; each round every run of equal blocks moves up one size with about half as many blocks, and a fresh run
explorer.verdict: It halts, proved in Coq (theorem halt : halts tm c0 on busycoq's definitions, no axioms). With E and F exchanged its table is 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1RA0LE_0LB0LF_0RA--- except for D0, where a detour (1LE, then 0RA and 1RA) ends where that table's single step ends, or halts if the cell to the left holds a 1. So every halt of that table is a halt of this machine. That table, started in A, is DeepMind's fast engine of busycoq PR 93 changed for one transition (as for 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD---, the same table started in B), and it reaches a halting configuration after 350,227 engine steps, on a tape of about 23562 cells. What it does. The run is understood as a process on a list of blocks: each round halves the number of blocks of every size and moves them up one size. That description comes from simulation; Lean proves only the sweep rules the rounds are built from. The sister machine 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LF behaves the same way.
